integrations.woocommerce.knownIssues.blo.message: Block-based layout on the WooCommerce checkout page

The PayPay WooCommerce plugin is not compatible with the block-based checkout layout. If you are using this type of layout, payment methods will not appear on the checkout page. You need to switch the checkout section to the classic checkout mode. To do this, follow the steps below:
In the WordPress admin page, locate the checkout page and click edit.
After opening the page editor, you need to select the block associated with the payment methods.

If the checkout page uses the block-based layout, a notice will appear on the right panel of the editor. Click "Switch to classic layout" and then click "Update" to save the changes. Payment methods should now appear at checkout.

soap.index.intro1.message: This guide describes the requirements and steps needed for integration with PayPay for clients who want greater control over the payment process in their applications.

soap.index.intro2.message: It provides mechanisms to obtain payment references, make direct payments from the merchant's website, check payment status, and process payment confirmations.

soap.payments.index.scenario3.message: Generation of a reference payable via the PayPay homepage.

soap.webhooks.index.intro.message:
A webhook is a way to receive information via a web or HTTP callback when an event occurs.
This makes the webhook a convenient way for an application or system to receive real-time information from PayPay.

soap.webhooks.index.paymentConfirmed.message: The action is triggered when a payment is confirmed.

soap.webhooks.index.paymentConfirmedNote.message: Note: only applies to payments issued through this webservice.

soap.webhooks.index.paymentCancelled.message: The action is triggered when the merchant/user cancels a payment.

soap.webhooks.index.paymentRefunded.message: The action is triggered when the merchant refunds a payment.
